title: Creator Legacy Infrastructure Architecture™
intro: The comprehensive framework for infrastructure that preserves a body of work, its ownership, and its legacy.

nodes.prompt: How is the creative identity documented so it can be understood, applied, and carried forward by someone other than you?
What is the written statement of what this body of work is, and is not?
What is the complete, current picture of who owns what — copyrights, trademarks, master files, platform accounts, domains?
What legal or administrative gaps exist, and what is the plan to close each one?
Which systems from The Creator Operating System™ are documented well enough that someone else could run them?
What is the single point of failure in how this venture runs today — the one thing that stops if you stop?
If this body of work needed to continue without you — temporarily or permanently — who is positioned to carry it, and what would they need?
What decisions have you made (or need to make) about licensing, archiving, or transferring the work after you're no longer actively creating it?
What does this body of work contribute to the community, culture, or field it belongs to — beyond its commercial value?
How should that contribution be described for someone encountering the work after you?
This body of work exists to …
It is owned and documented in …
It can be carried forward by …
What I want it to leave behind is …

closing.prompt: The one change we will make next, who will own it, and by when:
